newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus, World Bank deal won't lead to fast cash.
newsitem.headline: Belarus, World Bank deal won't lead to fast cash.

text.p: Belarus and the World Bank signed an agreement on mutual understanding, but the deal will not lead to an instant monetary injection for the former Soviet republic, Bank representative Christopher Willoughby said on Friday.
He said the signing was important for Belarus because it could serve as a catalyst to speed economic reforms.
After board approval of the agreement, missions would visit the former Soviet republic to begin talks on energy and water projects, he said.
World Bank credits have totalled $170 million in the nearly six years since Belarus became independent from the Soviet Union.

The agreement comes after statements earlier this week by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which said it would maintain relations with Belarus but said Minsk would have to reform economically if it hoped to renew credits frozen last year.
The Fund issued a statement earlier this week saying Belarus, whose economy has fallen under increasing government control, did not practice policies which could be supported by the Fund.
"There are concrete actions that need to be taken in order to begin negotiations on a program that can be supported by the IMF," the statement said.
Belarus has fallen far behind in economic reforms and still maintains strict state control over much of the economy.
